title: Component data for exterior presheaf under open pullback
statement: For a scheme X, an O_X-module M, a natural number n and an open U, there are component isomorphisms between the presheaf pullback of the sectionwise exterior-power presheaf and the sectionwise exterior-power presheaf of M.restrict U.ι, satisfying presheaf naturality.

proof.text: Define restriction of arbitrary module presheaves to image opens, with scalar transport through the inverse of the open immersion section isomorphisms. Construct its adjunction to presheaf pushforward explicitly: the unit is restriction along image(preimage(V)) <= V and the counit uses preimage(image(V)) = V. Check linearity using Scheme.Hom.app_appIso_inv and Scheme.Hom.appIso_inv_app_presheafMap, and naturality and both triangle identities using presheaf identity and composition laws. Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq identifies this explicit restriction with PresheafOfModules.pullback.

For any commutative-ring isomorphism R ≅ S and R-module A, construct mutually inverse maps between the S-scalar transport of the exterior power over R and the exterior power over S of the transported module. Construct each alternating map on tuples and extend it by exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv. The ring-isomorphism identities give the requisite scalar laws. Pure-wedge formulas and exteriorPower.ιMulti_span show that the two composites are identities; use span induction to retain pure-wedge extensionality after scalar transport.

Apply these component isomorphisms to the section modules of M. Test naturality on pure wedges: exteriorSheafRestriction_existsUnique sends each tuple to the wedge of its restricted sections, and both scalar-transport maps preserve that tuple formula. Thus naturality reduces to the defining restriction formula of M.restrict. Assemble a presheaf isomorphism using PresheafOfModules.isoMk, compose with the adjunction comparison, and evaluate it at each open to obtain the requested family and naturality equation.

proof_origin.note: The existing component-map route is implemented completely in Lean. The presheaf adjunction follows the formulas of Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.restrictAdjunction; scalar transport uses the exterior-power universal property and pure-wedge span. All local helpers are proved.

lean.statement: theorem exteriorPresheaf_open_pullback_data {X : Scheme.{v}} (M : X.Modules) (n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) : ∃ (app : ∀ V : U.toScheme.Opensᵒᵖ, ((PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} U.ι.toRingCatSheafHom.hom).obj (exteriorSheafPresheaf M n)).obj V ≅ (exteriorSheafPresheaf (M.restrict U.ι) n).obj V), ∀ {V W : U.toScheme.Opensᵒᵖ} (f : V ⟶ W), ((PresheafOfModules.pullback.{v} U.ι.toRingCatSheafHom.hom).obj (exteriorSheafPresheaf M n)).map f ≫ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.obj.map f).hom)).map (app W).hom = (app V).hom ≫ (exteriorSheafPresheaf (M.restrict U.ι) n).map f
